item.text: Findings: 1. **Incorrect first page offset** — [`src/users.js:5`]( /private/var/folders/r3/gtmdzdhn7138rqntsg15l6980000gn/T/atlas-bench-t4-review-CEkwCY/src/users.js:5) `page` is documented as 1-based, but `page * size` treats it as 0-based. `paginate(items, 1, 2)` returns items 3–4 instead of items 1–2. Fix: ```js const start = (page - 1) * size; ``` 2. **Incorrect age calculation around birthdays** — [`src/users.js:11-12`]( /private/var/folders/r3/gtmdzdhn7138rqntsg15l6980000gn/T/atlas-bench-t4-review-CEkwCY/src/users.js:11) The implementation compares only birth and current years. Someone whose 18th birthday is tomorrow is incorrectly treated as an adult. Fix by comparing the full dates, for example: ```js const cutoff = new Date( today.getFullYear() - 18, today.getMonth(), today.getDate() ); return birthDate <= cutoff; ``` 3. **Incomplete HTML escaping enables XSS** — [`src/users.js:18-20`]( /private/var/folders/r3/gtmdzdhn7138rqntsg15l6980000gn/T/atlas-bench-t4-review-CEkwCY/src/users.js:18) `String.replace()` with string arguments replaces only the first occurrence of each character. A name containing multiple tags can leave later markup unescaped, and `userRow()` inserts the result into HTML. For example, a name such as ` ` produces an executable `` element. Fix by replacing all occurrences, preferably with a context-appropriate trusted escaping utility: ```js return String(text) .replace(/&/g, '&') .replace(//g, '>') .replace(/"/g, '"') .replace(/'/g, '''); ``` No files were changed.
